reference.title: Band Bent over Hip Extension
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching: hinged forward with the hands braced, a band from the hands to the working foot)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the leg goes back, inhale as it returns.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s back, 0.6 s hold, 1.4 s return

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: pick a band you can push back fully for every rep without arching.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a stronger band; longer hold

cues.text: Hinge forward about 50 degrees with a flat back and brace both hands on a box, holding the band ends; loop the band round the right foot. Stand on the left leg, knee soft.
Breathe out and push the right leg straight back from the hip until it lines up with the trunk.
Squeeze the right glute for a moment; hips square, low back still.
Breathe in and let the band draw the leg back under the hip slowly.
Toes just off the floor, then repeat; switch legs after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to lift the leg higher
mistakes.fix: Stop when the leg lines up with the trunk; brace the stomach.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the hip open toward the ceiling
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones pointing at the floor.
Keep the working knee nearly straight and push through the heel.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the leg forward
mistakes.fix: Control the return over about 1.5 s.

kinematics.norm: From hip flexion under the hinged trunk to about neutral or a little past it (rig limit 20 degrees of extension) (clinical opinion)
The working thigh travels from under the hip to about in line with the trunk (clinical opinion)
Hip hinge with a flat back, trunk about 45-60 degrees forward and still, hands braced (clinical opinion)
Moving knee straight; stance knee soft (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled with a short hold (clinical opinion)
Elastic tension rises as the band stretches, so the load is highest with the leg back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band Bent over Hip Extension, video (movement reference)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Stop if pain in the low back, hip or knee, numbness or tingling occurs.
Check the band for nicks before use and keep it looped securely round the foot so it cannot slip off.
Band tension is user-chosen: start light.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low-back discomfort: hinge less and shorten the range.
progressions: 2 s hold with the leg back.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Moving-leg hip extensor. Glute cues and abdominal bracing raised gluteus maximus activity in body-weight hip extension exercises (Macadam 2019).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension with the knee straight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Stance-leg abductor holding the pelvis level on one leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the low back from arching as the leg goes back; a lumbopelvic control strategy raised gluteus maximus activity in related exercises (Macadam 2019).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the flat back in the hinge; they should not take over by arching (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the flat back in the hinge; they should not take over by arching (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Brace the arm on the box.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Brace the arm on the box.
